title: A route guard compares the request path to a literal and fails open on any mismatch, while the framework still routes appended segments to the same handler
index_line: T-0083 · AUTH_DECISION · exact-equality path guard vs framework PathInfo routing: /SetupWizard.aspx/ reaches the setup wizard after setup · dotnet · corroborated
invariant_violated: The guard assumed 'the request path equals /SetupWizard.aspx' and 'the request will be served by SetupWizard.aspx' are the same question. They are not: the guard compares the raw path with exact equality, while the routing layer maps an appended segment (or trailing slash) to the same handler — and the guard's deny branch only runs on equality, so every non-matching spelling fails open.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated GET requests /SetupWizard.aspx/ (a trailing slash or an appended path segment) on an instance that is already configured
the framework splits the path into the mapped page (FilePath) and the remainder (PathInfo) and still dispatches the request to SetupWizard.aspx
the guard compares the request path to the literal string with exact equality; the appended segment makes the comparison false
the false comparison is read as 'this is not the setup wizard', so the deny branch is skipped and the request continues to the handler
the setup wizard renders on an already-configured instance, letting the attacker create a new administrator account without credentials
with administrative access the attacker uploads an extension whose archive member path escapes the extension directory (CVE-2024-1708), dropping an executable into App_Extensions for code execution

source.http.request.value: the request path itself — /SetupWizard.aspx/ or /SetupWizard.aspx/<anything>, unauthenticated

guard.pipeline.value: the request-path equality check that gates the setup wizard (a deny-on-match guard, i.e. fail-open by construction)

sink.file.write.value: the administrative extension-upload path, where an archive member name (CVE-2024-1708) escapes the extension directory

encoding.path.value: the path-segment/PathInfo encoding difference between what the guard reads and what the router matches

preconditions.expr: the web interface answers and /SetupWizard.aspx is routed

check.spec: for p in /SetupWizard.aspx /SetupWizard.aspx/ '/SetupWizard.aspx/x'; do printf '%s ' "$p"; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "http://HOST$p"; done

preconditions.expr: the build predates 23.9.8 (the added ISetupHandler check)
the differing status between the exact path and an appended-segment path reflects a guard mismatch, not a redirect to login

check.spec: curl -s -i http://HOST/SetupWizard.aspx | head -5; curl -s -i http://HOST/SetupWizard.aspx/ | head -5

success: the exact path returns 302/redirect while the appended-segment path returns 200 with the setup form
the wizard accepts a new administrator on an instance that already has one
failure_like: both spellings return the same redirect or 404
the guard resolves the path and compares canonical handler identity instead of a string
false_positive: a 200 that is the login page is not the wizard — require the setup form and a created account
a trailing-slash redirect (301) is normal HTTP behaviour, not a bypass

hazards: any 'if path == X then check' guard in a framework that routes by prefix or by mapped handler
the fail-open shape is the real lesson: the guard denies on match, so the attacker only needs a spelling that is not equal
appended-segment routing exists in ASP.NET PathInfo, Tomcat path parameters, Spring suffix patterns, and nginx alias prefixes
non_transfers: routers that reject unmatched paths before the guard
guards that compare the resolved handler/module identity rather than the raw string

evidence.target: ConnectWise ScreenConnect 23.9.7 and earlier — SetupWizard path guard (CVE-2024-1709) with companion write CVE-2024-1708

provenance.author: Huntress Labs
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2024-1709: SetupWizard.aspx compares the request path to the literal /SetupWizard.aspx; if the path does not match, the setup wizard is allowed regardless of setup state, and .NET passes trailing path segments (/SetupWizard.aspx/anything) to the same handler; CVE-2024-1708 is the companion path-traversal write into App_Extensions

provenance.author: Horizon3.ai Attack Research Team
provenance.corroborates: independent deep dive on CVE-2024-1709: string.Equals exact-equality check on the request URL, so <app_url>/SetupWizard.aspx/ does not match while still resolving to SetupWizard.aspx; reproduces the 302 vs 200 difference between the two paths
